newsitem.title: JAPAN: Explosion damages home of Japan official.
newsitem.headline: Explosion damages home of Japan official.

text.p: An explosion damaged the home of a Japanese Transport Ministry official early on Monday and police said they suspect leftist radicals opposed to the expansion of Tokyo's Narita airport were responsible.
A police spokesman said an explosive device planted inside the garage at the Tokyo home of the official went off 4.15 a.m. on Monday.
No one was killed or injured in the explosion, which damaged a garage roof, doors of two cars and a house gate, he said.
"It is highly possible that members of a certain leftist group who oppose the expansion of Narita international airport planted the explosive device," he said. "Investigations are under way."
Police found parts of an alarm clock that was believed to have been used as a timing device.

The expansion of Narita airport, which opened in 1978, drew a furious response from leftist activists who supported local farmers' claims that the government improperly seized their land to build the airport.
